title: [MIG-008] Prove portable installed-consumer parity and publish the migration candidate
objective: Produce the evidence-backed immutable Vibez candidate that Fantasy Football can safely adopt.
inScope: Build a conformance harness that consumes only the actual packed artifact in a clean separate Git repository/workspace. Make the source checkouts unavailable on the module path and prohibit deep imports/copying core schemas. Include a non-npm project profile plus task requirements, affected/dependency contracts and varying required review-role subsets.

Exercise library and CLI from task loading through start, validation, independent role handling, rework, PR/CI/readiness, controlled merge and DONE reconciliation, plus status/explain/recovery/compatibility surfaces. Cover rejection side effects and uncertain outcomes.

Run the support matrix agreed in MIG-002, including Windows/PowerShell and POSIX, paths with spaces, alternate cwd and overlapping task IDs across two projects. Preserve existing full suites/schema checks/adversarial guards. Declare untested OS/filesystems unsupported.

Finish the source-delta checkpoint: verify #78/#76 and every accepted reusable source fix is present in Vibez or explicitly excluded with rationale. No ongoing product code fork is allowed after this checkpoint.

Publish an immutable versioned release candidate via the agreed channel with integrity/provenance, compatibility matrix, changelog, installation and upgrade/rollback docs. No public npm release absent that recorded decision.
**Expected surfaces:** Consumer conformance fixtures/harness, CI portability/pack jobs, release workflow/artifacts, migration evidence report and operator docs.
outOfScope: No Fantasy Football deletion/cutover, new UI or blanket claim of live independent review from fake-provider fixture results.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-01: Supported JS/types/CLI/assets and complete current workflow pass from a clean installed artifact without source checkout access.
AC-02: At least two independent project roots are isolated; a non-npm consumer uses only configured validators.
AC-03: Happy path, role/revision/CI rejection, failed review/rework, duplicate attempts, restart and uncertain merge outcomes preserve current guarantees.
AC-04: Source-delta reconciliation is complete and the artifact maps to a reviewed destination SHA and checksum.
AC-05: The release candidate is downloadable/installable through the agreed channel; fresh maintainer install/configure/diagnose/rollback instructions are exercised.
AC-06: Fixtures, live feature evidence and untested limitations are clearly distinguished in the acceptance report.
validationPlan:
Run destination build/full tests/schema validations/adversarial checks and the complete installed-artifact conformance suite on the declared platform matrix. Inspect the package payload and acceptance-to-evidence mapping; independent QA, Architecture and UAT review the same candidate revision.

Use applicable repository build/test/schema/contract checks. Retain exact commands/results, package/source/config identities and an acceptance-to-evidence map. Existing or fake-provider fixtures are not independent live review or task-completion evidence. This task is normal feature work, not a new canary requirement.
npm run build; npm test; python schemas/validate_fixtures.py; python schemas/validate_repository_contracts.py; npm run test:adversarial:mutations. Add issue-specific checks before admission.
